notes: **2026-09-02 (concurrency + scheduling pass)** — (branch `feat/bug-registry`, PR #597; `scripts/campaign/bugs.mjs` + `scripts/team/team.mjs` + SKILL.md, 3 code commits, one per blocker of the adversarial verify pass; self-test 107 → 129 checks) — **THREE DESIGN DEFECTS THE MECHANICAL PASS COULD NOT SEE, ALL OF THEM SILENT.** (1) THE SHARD LOCK: `upsertLedgerRow` was a read-modify-write with no lock, and the campaign runs sub-agents in parallel on one batch — two of them proving DIFFERENT rows of one `F##.jsonl` each read the whole shard and each wrote their own copy back, so the second erased the first; the verify pass reverted an already-proven, evidence-backed row to `queued` with BOTH gates green, because every write path asserts only its OWN row. Every shard read-modify-write now runs inside a `<shard>.lock` DIRECTORY (`withShardLock`, `mkdir` — atomic and loud on NTFS and POSIX, no new dependency), with the READ inside the hold or the caller's patch is already stale: `prove`/`discharge`/`reopen`/`claim`/`release`/`tier` each wrap their own read→judge→write region and `upsertLedgerRow` takes it again re-entrantly; `move` takes BOTH shards via `withShardLocks` in sorted order so two opposite moves cannot deadlock; a hold spins 2s at 20ms, breaks a lock older than 5s with a stderr note, and is released from a process `exit` handler as well as `finally` (`fail()` calls `process.exit`, which does not unwind). (2) WAVE OCCUPANCY: claiming a batch DELETED the constraints it carried — `computeWaves` coloured only `candidates` (every in-flight/leased batch already removed) and the conflict graph treated an `in-flight` row as CLOSED, so after claiming F11 `deps` no longer reported F11<->F12 and `next` offered F12 to a second agent editing the same two web files. A busy batch is now a PRE-COLOURED OCCUPANT of wave 1: it holds a slot of the agent cap, keeps its hard conflicts, and is never returned as a pick; `CONFLICTING` (= WORKABLE + `in-flight`) is what `batchConflicts` and `deps` filter on; `selectBatches` returns `busy` and `blocked`, `next` prints `blocked by in-flight F## — shares <file>` among its skipped reasons, and both `--json` payloads carry them — so wave 1 can legitimately be shorter than the cap, or empty. (3) CLAIM-GRAMMAR PARITY: `liveClaim` re-implemented `team.mjs`'s grammar and diverged on all three rules, every time the dangerous way — `--jq .[].body` flattened comment boundaries (destroying the marker filter), and `/^\s*(claim|release):/` allowed leading whitespace where team.mjs anchors `^claim:`/`^release:` with /m; one UNMARKED `claim:` comment shut the dispatcher down for every batch, and an unmarked OR indented `release:` freed a lease `team.mjs claim` still refuses with "held by …". Comments are now fetched structured (`--jq "[.[]|{body}]"`), parsed per COMMENT, marker-filtered before any parse, matched with team.mjs's own two regexes verbatim, and extracted as a pure `readClaims(comments)`; BOTH files carry a warning naming the other and listing the three rules — they must change together, in one commit. Every fix drives the REAL command and each was MUTATION-PROBED: removing the lock turns "BOTH rows landed" red, reverting either half of the occupancy fix turns 5 checks red, and restoring the old grammar turns exactly the three refuted cases red. New test seam `BUGS_TEST_STALL_MS` makes the lost-update race deterministic instead of hoped-for; the concurrency check drives two REAL child processes over `Promise.all(spawn)` via a small orchestrator, because the self-test is synchronous. || History in CHANGELOG.md (this directory).
